turns.content: A right triangle ABC is right-angled at B, with AB=n(n+1) and hypotenuse AC=(n+1)(n+4), where n is a positive integer. Use the Pythagorean theorem to simplify BC^2.
From that factorization, give a necessary and sufficient perfect-square condition for BC to be an integer.
Justify both directions of the equivalence by separating the factor that is already a square from the remaining factor.
Parametrize all positive integers n satisfying the square condition, introducing an integer parameter k.
Check the parametrization in both directions and determine the smallest allowed value of k from n>0.
Impose the restriction n<100000 seconds on the parametrization and find the complete integer range of k.
Count the resulting positive integers n for which BC is integral.
